properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Two of Alex's Opportunities, 2026-08-14 (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md), kept together because they are one question asked of two tools — and separable if the answer differs.

HIS WORDS. On detect_gaps: "Scoped `detect_gaps`: filter to gaps whose `affected_ids` include the seed (or its SATISFIES/REALIZES neighbors), and do not raise `unverified_capability` for `planned` + zero artifacts." On loop_status: "`loop_status` session mode: 'building this Capability' hides unsurfaced project-wide gaps unless they touch the seed."

⭐ THE SHARPENING, AND IT CHANGES THE QUESTION: SCOPING IS NOT MISSING. `cap:scoped-analysis` is built and shipped — "A team asks the detectors about its own part, and is told what it did not see" (`chg:scoped-analysis-built`), and `loop_status` already takes a `contributor_id`. So this is not a request for a feature that does not exist. It is a report that THE FEATURE THAT EXISTS DID NOT HELP: he called `detect_gaps(scope: Capability)` at depth 1, 2 and 3, got `in_scope` of roughly 47–51 every time, "almost every hit `unverified_capability` on unrelated planned work", and still could not answer "is THIS Capability still in an `unrealized_capability` gap?" without grepping `affected_ids` by hand.

THAT REFRAMES IT: the scope is computed by GRAPH REACHABILITY, and on a connected design a few hops reaches most of it. The question is whether scope should mean "what the seed can reach" or "what is actually about the seed".

THE OPTIONS:

(a) FILTER BY `affected_ids` — exactly his proposal: a gap is in scope when the seed (or its SATISFIES/REALIZES neighbours) is in the gap's own affected set. CHEAP, and it answers the question he actually had. COUNTER: it narrows to gaps that already name the seed, so a gap about a neighbour that WILL matter to him drops out — and `cap:scoped-analysis`'s whole promise is that it "names what it did not see", which this makes both more necessary and more voluminous.

(b) SUPPRESS `unverified_capability` FOR `planned` + ZERO ARTIFACTS — his second clause, and independently useful. CHEAP. COUNTER: it is a phase judgement baked into a detector, and this project's standing preference is to report the fact and let the reader judge (`dec:report-dont-judge`). It may also be the same finding as `dec:should-a-design-be-able-to-say-it-describes-something-that-already-exists`, one layer along — a design that has not started building does not want build gaps at all.

(c) A SESSION MODE ON `loop_status` — "I am building this Capability". Answers the noise complaint where he actually felt it: `next[0]` was detect-and-ask all session while the work was implement → user-correct → implement. COUNTER, and it is serious: `loop_status`'s contract is that a scoped answer must never read as "the design is clean" — it already keeps unattributable debt under `scope.not_attributable` for exactly this reason. A mode that HIDES project-wide gaps is the one thing that contract forbids, so this option must be built as "rank differently", not "hide".

(d) DO NOTHING TO THE TOOLS; THE COMPLAINT IS ABOUT PHASE — he was mid-bugfix with a user watching a broken app, and reflow2 has no notion of that. His items 3 and 9 are the same complaint from the other side. COUNTER: "wait for a phase model" has been the answer to several of these, and nothing is scheduled.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether depth was the wrong control or scope was the wrong concept; and whether 47–51 in_scope on his design is large relative to the design's size, which nobody measured.
properties.name: IDEA — scoped detection is BUILT and a real session still could not ask "is this one Capability still in a gap?". Should scope filter by relevance rather than by reachability, and should loop_status get a session mode?
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Two ideas held in one node because they are one question asked of two surfaces; noted inside that they can be answered apart if the answer differs. The reframing — that scoping exists and did not narrow — is a finding, not a decision, and is stated as such.
